anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs keep all three facts: the helper's `open - contract exception` return leaves HEAD at pre_wave_head, triggers no pre-push review or push, leaves both grants intact, and the rendered menu offers accept-via-owning-process, preserve-contract-with-repair, show evidence, and stop, with no description edit proposed anywhere. Nothing in After moved a fact; the differences are additive and consistent with the Change: After records the helper result path in the exception, adds the scoped-test pass-before-commit rule and the no-rebase/no-force-push rule to the helper task, and extends the menu footer with "revoke fix" / "revoke merge base" compose options. One wording point worth keeping consistent for other cases: After's `repair.wave` stores `pushed_head: null` while Before stores the pre-wave head; `null` is the better reading for an unpushed wave and should be the canonical form so later wave-push and stale-proposal cases key off a real pushed SHA. Also, since the Change makes description corrections flow through fix picks/retained grants, it would help to state explicitly in the contract-exception overlay that no description payload is minted for a pending exception, so f3 is visibly guaranteed rather than inferred from silence.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both outputs already satisfy all three facts: the helper's `open - contract exception` return halts repair with no further implementer, review, tests, push, or scope edit despite the held `fix` and `merge base` grants; the rendered menu offers `accept contract change` via the owning amendment process, `preserve contract` with resumed implementation repair, and `stop`; and neither output touches the PR body or proposes a description correction in place of an amendment. After adds useful precision (explicit `gauntlet_setting` cap read, named subagent call, recorded `pre_wave_head`, and the sentence that the pending contract exception takes precedence over retained repair routing), which makes the stop reasoning more legible. Nothing moved; to keep it that way while delivering the Change, make sure the new description-correction routing is explicitly subordinate to a pending contract exception—e.g. a line such as 'a pending contract exception suspends every retained repair action, including description corrections, until the amendment decision is made'—so that the `fix`-grant-applies-description-payloads rule can never be read as licensing a body rewrite that paraphrases the dropped constant-time requirement.
